title: A White House meeting, a tanker off Qatar, and drones over Ryazan
summary: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian envoys as talks open in Brussels and the Komyshuvakha toll rises to forty, mediators push a blockade-for-Hormuz framework after a tanker is hit north of Qatar, Ukraine hits Ryazan and an Ozon warehouse, and the Theodore Roosevelt heads west.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Thursday, November fifth. And today there's a lot of diplomacy around the Russia–Ukraine war, alongside the fighting.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's start at the White House. First Lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian representatives there today. It's a pretty unusual diplomatic role for a first lady.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The focus was that local ceasefire around Oleshky, the occupied town in Kherson region. She praised both sides for choosing, in her words, humanity over war. And President Trump said the mission delivered aid and allowed the evacuation of nearly eight hundred people.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Ukraine's foreign minister had described really dire conditions in Oleshky. He said some residents were eating grass and weeds, with no medicine, clean water or electricity.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And it's not the only diplomatic track. Technical talks on Ukraine's post-war reconstruction and security guarantees also began today in Brussels. And trilateral talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine are due in the United Arab Emirates next week.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: NBC notes all this is happening while Ukraine's relations with Washington are at a low point. So there's a lot riding on these meetings.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the fighting didn't pause for any of it. There's a grim update on Monday's strike in Komyshuvakha, in Zaporizhzhia region. That's where Russian guided bombs hit a school being used as an aid centre.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Zelensky had put the toll at thirty-three on Tuesday. bne IntelliNews now reports it has risen to forty. Zelensky has called it one of the deadliest attacks of the war.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Overnight, Russia's attack was smaller than earlier this week. Ukraine's air force says Russia launched a hundred and twenty-eight drones and two Kh-thirty-five cruise missiles. A hundred and five of the drones were stopped.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Drones hit the cities of Dnipro and Samar, injuring three people. A logistics site in the Kyiv region was set on fire. And Kyiv Post reports one woman was killed.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Ukraine, meanwhile, sent more than two hundred drones at Russia's Ryazan region overnight. The governor says falling debris started fires at industrial sites and cut power to parts of the city.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Ukrainian monitoring channels claim the Ryazan oil refinery was hit. Officials haven't confirmed that. Russia says it shot down about five hundred drones in total overnight.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the day before, drones hit a big logistics centre for the online retailer Ozon in Adygeysk, in southern Russia. Ozon said the site would temporarily stop operating.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line, the General Staff reported a hundred and eighty-four clashes on Wednesday. The Pokrovsk sector was busiest, with seventeen Russian attacks, and ten more around Kostiantynivka.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Let's turn to the Gulf. Late on Wednesday, the British maritime agency UKMTO said a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles, about fifty nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, at the northern tip of Qatar.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The crew's condition and the extent of the damage weren't confirmed. And notice the location. That's well inside the Gulf, not in the strait itself. Earlier this week there were also hits off the Saudi coast and south of Lavan Island.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So the attacks are spread across the Gulf, not just at the strait.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the diplomatic side, officials say Qatari mediators are now pushing a fairly simple framework. Iran would stop its attacks in the strait, and in return the US would lift its blockade of Iranian ports.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: But Iran says Hormuz stays shut until all its demands are met. That's the blockade, sanctions relief and frozen funds. And reports say senior US officials are split. Some favour strikes, others, including the CIA director and the Treasury secretary, favour keeping up economic pressure.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Which matches what we heard after the midterms. Iran's speaker said Americans voted no to war, and Trump said the war ends when he says it ends.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Quick lap of the other fronts. Sudan. Ethiopia has expelled six Sudanese diplomats. That's after Sudan complained to the UN Security Council and the African Union, accusing Ethiopia of hosting launch sites for Rapid Support Forces drones.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the CFR tracker, citing Sudans Post, reports the Rapid Support Forces and allied militias captured the Sali military base in Blue Nile state. That's in Sudan's southeast.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Yemen, Al Jazeera reports heavy fighting in al-Jawf governorate between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And now the ships. The Theodore Roosevelt is still listed in the South China Sea. But satellite imagery and flight-tracking data reported today suggest the carrier group is heading west, toward the Middle East.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush remain in the Arabian Sea. And in the Atlantic, RANE's naval map lists both the Nimitz and the Eisenhower underway. The Nimitz is training ahead of its retirement in twenty twenty-seven, and the Eisenhower is doing pre-deployment work-ups.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. Whether the blockade-for-Hormuz idea goes anywhere, or whether the US chooses strikes instead. The trilateral Ukraine talks in the UAE next week. And whether the Roosevelt shows up in the Indian Ocean.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
